findings.claim: The change introduces concrete daemon/package data directory examples, violating the repository rule forbidding concrete daemon data path examples.
findings.evidence: Constraint: "Daemon data paths derive from `RUNTIME_DATA_DIR`. Do not introduce concrete filesystem examples for the daemon data directory..."; hunk adds `Set OD_DATA_DIR to an absolute path (for example, C:\\Users\\You\\${compactName} on Windows or /Users/you/${compactName} on macOS/Linux) ...`.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the concrete filesystem examples from the OD_DATA_DIR error text and describe the requirement generically.

findings.claim: The MCP server name is resolved at module import time instead of call/runtime time, so a profile applied after import can leave KnowDesign advertising `open-design`.
findings.evidence: Acceptance criteria require brand values be "resolved at call time not import time"; the hunk defines `const SERVER_NAME = defaultMcpServerName();` at top level.
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve the server name inside the MCP server creation/start path, or expose a function that calls `defaultMcpServerName()` when the server is instantiated.

findings.claim: The headless packaged entry resolves brand identity from `process.env` without applying the baked build profile, so a no-environment KnowDesign launch can still use Open Design identity.
findings.evidence: Acceptance criteria: "the knowdesign brand follows OD_BUILD_PROFILE=knowdesign and is also BAKED into the packaged config so a launch with no environment variable is knowdesign" and "D-020: profile baked by construction"; the only new baked-profile application is in `apps/packaged/src/config.ts` inside `readPackagedConfig()`, while `apps/packaged/src/headless.ts` uses `resolveBrand(process.env).slug` in the catch path and `resolveHeadlessNamespaceBaseRoot()` uses `resolveBrand(env).slug` without any baked-profile application in the headless entry.
findings.suggested_fix: Ensure the headless entry reads the packaged config and calls `applyBakedBuildProfile(raw.buildProfile)` before any `resolveBrand(...)` or brand-derived path/name is used.

findings.claim: Brand-derived OD_DATA_DIR error text ignores the function's `env` parameter and reads `process.env`, producing the wrong brand when callers pass an explicit environment.
findings.evidence: The hunk is inside `resolvePackagedDataRoot(..., env)` but uses `const productName = resolveBrand(process.env).productName;` instead of `resolveBrand(env)`.
